PASSED IN MVC NO.109/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL DISTRICT JUDGE AND ADDITIONAL MACT, UDUPI (SITTING AT KUNDAPURA), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This is an appeal filed by the claimants aggrieved by the award passed in MVC No.109/2016 dated 21.06.2017 seeking enhancement of the compensation.

2. It is the case of the claimant that, on 26.09.2015 at about 1.45 pm when the claimant was walking by the side of the dambar road from Kalthodu towards Kambadakone side, at that time a motorcycle riding by its rider came from Kalthodu towards Kambadakone side in a rash and negligent manner,
took the said vehicle to the extreme left side of the road and dashed against the claimant, who was walking on the mud NC: 2023:KHC:37633 road.
Due to the said impact, he sustained grievous injuries.

As per the wound certificate he sustained the following injuries:
1. Head injury mild haemorrhagic contusion in left contrum ascmiovable,
2. Nasole bone fracture,
3. Distal femoral condyle fracture right,
4. Abrasion on right foot 5.
Right knee swollen- painful.
3. As per the wound certificate, injury Nos.1 to 3 are grievous in nature and injury Nos. 4 and 5 are simple in nature.
The Court below had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Then basing on the medical bills placed before the Court below an amount of Rs.68,510/- was granted.
Towards medical expenses, towards future medical expenses an amount of Rs.16,000/- was granted.

When it comes to the disability the doctor had opined that he had sustained NC:
2023:KHC:37633 26% disability to his right lower limb. However the Court below considering the income tax returns filed by him i.e., Exs.P10 and P11 has come to the conclusion that, the claimant could not place any evidence to show that because of these injuries there was loss of income to the Sri Sudhakara Shetty vs Sri Nagaraja on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113920408/
2 claimant and granted an amount of Rs.50,000/- under the head of loss of discomfort.

sentences.text:
Then coming to the loss of earning the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.8,069/-, considering Rs.620/-
per day for the hospitalization period.
Towards conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges granted an amount of Rs.8,000/-.
Altogether compensation of an amount of Rs.2,10,580/- was granted by the Tribunal.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that when he had suffered the disability of 26% towards the limb, the Court below ought to have considered disability considering the income of the claimant who is the income tax assesse.
It is submitted that for the three simple injuries sustained by him the NC: 2023:KHC:37633 Court below had granted only an amount of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Learned counsel submits that even under the heads of loss of earning during the laid up period and loss of amenities and conveyance the amounts granted by the Tribunal were not reasonable.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that in every case of disability the claimant is not entitled for compensation under the head of future loss of income unless and until there is functional disability which would have impact on his future earnings.
In this case the material placed on records shows that there is no loss of income and the future aspects of the claimants are not affected.
The Court below rightly not granted the future loss of income by applying the multiplier.

It is submitted that by granting an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards discomfort,
whatever the inconvenience that is caused to the claimant had been rightly compensated.
Learned counsel submits that under all the heads the amount that were granted are NC: 2023:KHC:37633 reasonable, no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.
6. Having heard learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
7. First coming to the head of pain and suffering the Court below had observed that as per the wound certificate there are three grievous injuries and two simple injuries.
The accident is of the year 2015.
Considering the pain and sufferings this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.1,20,000/- towards pain and suffering.

Towards medical bills and future medical expenses the court below had granted an amount of Rs.68,510/- and 16,000/- respectively, basing on the evidence and no interference is called for under these heads.
Then coming to the loss of income during the laid up period, considering the injuries atleast he requires three months time to get back to the work.

Considering Rs.10,000/- per month this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.30,000/- for three months, towards loss NC: 2023:KHC:37633 of discomfort the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.50,000/- which is reasonable and no interference is called for.

Towards conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges under these three heads the Court below had granted an amount of Rs.8,000/- and considering the evidence on record this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.15,000/- under the said head.
8. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA -vs- M.MALATHI AND ANOTHER1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.
All together the claimant entitled is for amount of Rs.3,09,510/-.

i) Accordingly, the Appeal is partly allowed, enhancing the compensation amount from Rs.2,10,580/- to Rs.3,09,510/-.
ii) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
iii) The respondent - insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the NC: 2023:KHC:37633 judgment.
On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing any security.
iv) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
v) No costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
